# ethereum-optimism/design-docs Weekly Report (Apr 12 - 18, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week, design and troubleshooting efforts focused on refining the L2 architecture and addressing critical node synchronization issues affecting the Superchain. Key discussions centered on the long-term roadmap for the L2 Function Module Architecture (FMA) and the prioritization of gas introspection changes for upcoming network upgrades. Meanwhile, active investigation continues into a synchronization bug in `op-node` that has impacted production environments like Base Mainnet, highlighting a shift toward protocol stability and reliability.

## 🛠️ Key Developments
While no new pull requests were finalized during this period, the technical focus remained on architectural planning and refining existing protocol specifications.

### Protocol Upgrades & Roadmap Planning
The team is currently evaluating the timeline for protocol changes across different upgrade cycles. A significant focus was placed on the **CrossL2Inbox**, specifically regarding the removal of gas introspection. It was determined that this change is not a prerequisite for the "Glamsterdam Defense" milestone but will become critical for the subsequent "Glamsterdam on L2" phase. This distinction allows the team to prioritize immediate security and stability fixes over non-critical architectural refactors.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage
The week's activity was dominated by high-priority troubleshooting and the initiation of new design threads for future Ethereum hardfork compatibility.

### New & Active Issues
*   **L2 Function Module Architecture (FMA):** A new design thread was opened to discuss the integration of "Osaka" features within the L2 FMA. This represents early-stage planning to ensure the OP Stack remains aligned with the broader Ethereum roadmap ([#374](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/374)).
*   **op-node Sync Failures:** A critical issue persists where `op-node` becomes stuck in Execution Layer (EL) sync mode upon restarting, specifically when using `reth` with existing synced data. This issue is a high priority as it has been observed blocking nodes on Base Mainnet. Current workarounds involve manually switching the sync mode from EL to Consensus Layer (CL) sync while contributors investigate the root cause ([#18468](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/18468)).
*   **CrossL2Inbox Refinement:** Ongoing discussion regarding the removal of gas introspection ([#19374](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19374)) has helped clarify the dependency graph for upcoming hardforks, ensuring that development resources are allocated to the most urgent protocol requirements.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was characterized by deep technical triage between protocol engineers and node operators. The active investigation into the `op-node` synchronization bug demonstrates a tight feedback loop between the core developers and ecosystem partners like Base. The discussions in the design-docs repository continue to serve as a vital clearinghouse for coordinating complex upgrades across the Superchain, ensuring that contributors are aligned on which changes are "blockers" versus "nice-to-haves" for upcoming releases.
